refinedGoal: Build Adrian v0.1.0: a self-hosted, opinionated ADR database daemon. A three-container Docker Compose stack (adrian / qdrant / embedder) on network `adrian`, with only Adrian exposing a port. Adrian is the system of record in SQLite, ingests MADR documents over REST, parses them into a typed section/item projection, chunks them along template semantics, embeds chunks with uibk-embedding-v1 served by a from-scratch Rust candle engine, and indexes them in Qdrant as ColBERT multivectors plus dense vectors for hybrid retrieval. Coding agents connect over streamable-HTTP MCP (plus a stdio proxy). CPU-only for v0.1.0 with a `cuda` cargo feature present but disabled. Out of scope for v0.1.0: clustering into decision points, bitemporal valid-time queries, scope decay tracking, multi-tenancy, auth beyond an optional static bearer token.

tasks.description: SQLite schema, migrations, and the store layer in adrian-core
tasks.contract:
Implement the SQLite persistence layer in crates/adrian-core. Source of truth for all records; Qdrant is a derived index only.

migrations/0001_init.sql must create exactly these tables. Use TEXT for UUIDs is NOT allowed: store ids as BLOB (16-byte uuid). Timestamps as INTEGER unix seconds. Dates (decided_on) as TEXT 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

  workspace(id BLOB PK, slug TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)
  project(id BLOB PK, workspace_id BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES workspace(id), slug TEXT NOT NULL, name TEXT NOT NULL,
          repo_url TEXT, default_template TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'madr',
          embed_model TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'uibk-embedding-v1', embed_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
          created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, UNIQUE(workspace_id, slug))
  adr(id BLOB PK, project_id BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES project(id), external_ref TEXT NOT NULL, number INTEGER,
      slug TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, created_by TEXT NOT NULL,
      cur_rev INTEGER NOT NULL, cur_status TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE(project_id, external_ref))
  adr_rev(adr_id BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES adr(id), rev INTEGER NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, template TEXT NOT NULL,
          source_format TEXT NOT NULL, source_bytes BLOB NOT NULL, source_sha256 BLOB NOT NULL,
          content_sha256 BLOB NOT NULL, decided_on TEXT, tx_from INTEGER NOT NULL, tx_to INTEGER,
          PRIMARY KEY(adr_id, rev))
  section(id BLOB PK, adr_id BLOB NOT NULL, rev INTEGER NOT NULL, parent_id BLOB, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
          raw_heading TEXT NOT NULL, ordinal INTEGER NOT NULL, text TEXT NOT NULL, option_key TEXT,
          byte_start INTEGER NOT NULL, byte_end INTEGER NOT NULL, content_sha256 BLOB NOT NULL)
  item(id BLOB PK, adr_id BLOB NOT NULL, rev INTEGER NOT NULL, section_id BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES section(id),
       kind TEXT NOT NULL, ordinal INTEGER NOT NULL, text TEXT NOT NULL, option_key TEXT,
       byte_start INTEGER NOT NULL, byte_end INTEGER NOT NULL)
  status_event(id BLOB PK, adr_id BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES adr(id), from_status TEXT, to_status TEXT NOT NULL,
               effective_from TEXT, recorded_at INTEGER NOT NULL, actor TEXT NOT NULL, reason TEXT, superseded_by BLOB)
  scope(adr_id BLOB NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, value TEXT NOT NULL, origin TEXT NOT NULL,
        confidence REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 1.0, PRIMARY KEY(adr_id, kind, value))
  technology(adr_id BLOB NOT NULL, canonical TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(adr_id, canonical, role))
  chunk(id BLOB PK, adr_id BLOB NOT NULL, rev INTEGER NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, ordinal INTEGER NOT NULL,
        section_id BLOB, text TEXT NOT NULL, text_sha256 BLOB NOT NULL, token_count INTEGER,
        truncated INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, UNIQUE(adr_id, rev, kind, ordinal))
  chunk_vector(chunk_id BLOB NOT NULL REFERENCES chunk(id), model TEXT NOT NULL, version INTEGER NOT NULL,
               collection TEXT NOT NULL, point_id BLOB NOT NULL, token_vectors INTEGER NOT NULL,
               dense INTEGER NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(chunk_id, model, version))
  embed_job(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, chunk_id BLOB NOT NULL, model TEXT NOT NULL, version INTEGER NOT NULL,
            role TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'document', state TEXT NOT NULL, attempts INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
            last_error TEXT, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL)
  ingest_request(project_id BLOB NOT NULL, idempotency_key TEXT NOT NULL, request_sha256 BLOB NOT NULL,
                 response_json TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(project_id, idempotency_key))
  chunk_fts -> FTS5 virtual table over chunk.text, content='chunk', content_rowid='rowid' is NOT usable with a BLOB PK;
               instead create `CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE chunk_fts USING fts5(text, chunk_id UNINDEXED, tokenize='unicode61')`
               and keep it in sync from application code inside the same transaction.

INDEXES required: adr(project_id, cur_status), adr(project_id, number), chunk(adr_id, rev), embed_job(state, id), scope(kind, value), status_event(adr_id, recorded_at).

STATUS VOCABULARY (closed set, enforced in Rust): proposed | accepted | rejected | deprecated | superseded | withdrawn.

  - pragmas: journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, foreign_keys=ON, busy_timeout=5000, page_size=8192
  - create_workspace, ensure_default_workspace
  - create_project, get_project_by_slug, list_projects
  - insert_adr_with_revision(...) transactional: adr + adr_rev + sections + items + chunks + embed_jobs + fts rows
  - get_adr, get_adr_by_external_ref, list_adrs(project, status, limit, offset)
  - get_current_revision(adr_id), get_sections(adr_id, rev), get_items(adr_id, rev)
  - record_status_event(adr_id, to_status, actor, reason) which also updates adr.cur_status
  - list_status_events(adr_id)
  - set_scopes(adr_id, Vec<Scope>), set_technologies(adr_id, Vec<Technology>), get_scopes, get_technologies
  - list_chunks(adr_id, rev), get_chunk, chunk_by_id

  - record_chunk_vector(chunk_id, model, version, collection, point_id, token_vectors, dense)
  - search_lexical(project_id, query, limit) using chunk_fts with bm25 ranking, joined back to chunk/adr
  - store_ingest_response(project_id, key, sha, json), lookup_ingest_response(project_id, key) -> Option<(sha, json)>

Use `uuid::Uuid::new_v7()` for ids, `Uuid::new_v5(&Uuid::NAMESPACE_OID, name)` for deterministic chunk ids where the name is `adr_id||rev||kind||ordinal`.

tasks.description: MADR parser producing the typed section/item projection, with a real fixture corpus
tasks.contract:
Implement crates/adrian-core/src/parser/ producing the section/item projection defined in task-2 from MADR Markdown. This is the highest-quality-risk component: get it right with a real corpus.

INPUT: raw Markdown bytes of one ADR.
OUTPUT: ParsedAdr { title, template, decided_on, status_raw, decision_makers, consulted, informed, sections: Vec<ParsedSection>, items: Vec<ParsedItem>, warnings: Vec<ParseWarning> } where every section and item carries byte_start/byte_end into the ORIGINAL source bytes.

MADR STRUCTURE to support (full, minimal, annotated and bare variants):
  - Optional YAML front matter delimited by --- at byte 0. Parse with serde_yaml into a struct with fields status, date, decision-makers, consulted, informed, plus capture ALL other keys into a `extra: serde_yaml::Mapping` so nothing is lost. Values may be a string, a list, or a comma-separated string; normalize lists to Vec<String>. Empty values (e.g. `status:` with nothing) must parse as None, not as an error.
  - Title: the single H1 (`# ...`).
  - H2 sections and H3 subsections. Map headings to a closed kind set by case-insensitive, punctuation-insensitive matching of the heading text against known MADR headings, including these aliases:
      context|context and problem statement|problem statement -> context
      decision drivers|drivers|forces -> drivers
      considered options|options -> options
      decision outcome|outcome|decision -> outcome
      pros and cons of the options|pros and cons -> pros_cons
      more information|links|references -> more_info
    H3 under decision outcome: consequences -> consequences, confirmation -> confirmation.
    Anything unmatched -> other, keeping raw_heading verbatim.
  - Headings are located by a small Markdown-aware scanner, NOT by regex over lines: fenced code blocks (``` and ~~~) and HTML comments must not be treated as headings. Preserve fenced blocks verbatim inside section text.

ITEMS: extract list items from sections with kind in {drivers, options, consequences, pros_cons}:
  - In `options`: each top-level bullet is an option item, kind=option.
  - In `consequences`: bullets matching /^\s*\*?\s*Good,/ -> consequence_good; /Bad,/ -> consequence_bad; else consequence_other.
  - In `pros_cons`: bullets matching /^\s*\*?\s*Good,/ -> pro; /Bad,/ -> con; /Neutral,/ -> neutral.
  - In `drivers`: each bullet -> driver.
  - Strip leading list markers and trailing HTML comments from item text, but keep byte spans pointing at the original text including the marker.

OPTION JOIN (critical). MADR deliberately has no option identifiers (see MADR ADR-0006), so the option listed in `considered_options` and the H3 heading under `pros_cons` are related ONLY by title string equality. Implement:
  - `option_key(title) -> String` = 'opt:' + lowercase(trim(collapse_internal_whitespace(strip_surrounding_quotes(strip_trailing_punctuation(strip_markdown_emphasis(title)))))
  - Unicode-aware lowercasing and normalization of typographic quotes (‘’“”) and dashes to their ASCII equivalents BEFORE stripping punctuation.
  - H3 headings under pros_cons get the same option_key and their bullets inherit it.
  - Record a ParseWarning::UnmatchedOption when an option has no pros_cons entry and ParseWarning::OrphanProsCons when a pros_cons H3 has no matching option. Do NOT fail on either; both are common in real corpora.

FIXTURE CORPUS: commit at least 25 real MADR files under fixtures/madr/, downloaded from public repos in the adr GitHub org (adr/madr docs/decisions, adr/adr-log docs/adr, adr/gadr docs/adr, adr/ad-guidance-tool docs/adr, adr/madrlint docs). Record the source URL for each in fixtures/madr/SOURCES.md. Also hand-write at least 8 synthetic edge cases: minimal template, bare template, front matter absent, front matter with empty status, front matter with YAML list deciders, CRLF line endings, headings inside fenced code blocks, unicode/smart quotes in option titles, an ADR with no considered options, an ADR with an H3 in pros_cons that matches nothing.

Write a golden projection test: fixtures/madr/expected/<name>.json committed alongside, generated once by the parser and then reviewed by hand for at least 5 files, asserting the parser is stable against regressions. The test asserts equality, not similarity.

Worker MAY run `cargo test -p adrian-core parser` to iterate. Ensure zero panics on the whole corpus: a fuzz-ish test that feeds every fixture plus truncated prefixes of each fixture at every byte boundary must never panic.

tasks.description: Semantic chunker that turns the section/item projection into embedding chunks
tasks.contract:
Implement crates/adrian-core/src/chunker.rs. The ADR template IS the chunking scheme; do not use a generic text splitter.

Emit chunks with kind in a closed set: document | context | driver | option | outcome | consequence | confirmation | more_info.

COMPOSITION RULES:
  document   = full source text, truncated to the document token budget. Always exactly one per ADR.
  context    = the `context` section text. One per ADR, omitted if the section is absent or empty.
  driver     = one chunk per `driver` item.
  option     = one chunk per option, composed as: option title line, then the pros_cons section's description prose for that option_key, then ALL of that option's pro/con/neutral items as a bullet list. This composition is the whole point: a 3-word bullet alone is useless, and MADR keeps the title and the arguments in different sections joined only by title string equality.
  outcome    = the `outcome` section text including the justification.
  consequence= one chunk per `consequence_good` / `consequence_bad` / `consequence_other` item.
  confirmation = the `confirmation` section text.
  more_info  = the `more_info` section text.

ORDINALS: stable per (adr, kind). `document` and `context` and `outcome` and `confirmation` and `more_info` are always ordinal 0. `driver`, `option`, `consequence` ordinals follow source order starting at 0.

TOKEN BUDGET: chunks are budgeted at 2048 tokens for `document` and 256 tokens for every other kind (matching the embedder's document and query limits in task-6 are NOT relevant here; all chunks are embedded as documents, so the limit is 2048). Provide a `max_tokens` parameter defaulting to 2048. Use a token-counting function injected as a trait so tests can use a deterministic stub and production can use the real tokenizer via the embedder client. Do not hardcode a tokenizer in this crate.

OVERSIZE HANDLING: if a composed chunk exceeds max_tokens, split it on paragraph boundaries first, then on sentence boundaries, then hard-split, and emit multiple chunks with ordinals continuing. Set `truncated = 1` only when a single indivisible unit still exceeds the budget. Never silently drop text.

EMPTY HANDLING: never emit a chunk whose text is empty or whitespace-only.

DETERMINISM: chunk ids are uuid v5 over the name `{adr_id}||{rev}||{kind}||{ordinal}`. Given the same ADR revision the chunker must produce byte-identical ids and text. No HashMap iteration order may influence output; use BTreeMap or sort explicitly.

Also emit, per ADR: `scopes: Vec<Scope>` and `technologies: Vec<Technology>` extracted heuristically, each with origin='extracted' and a confidence value:
  - scopes: backtick-quoted path-like strings (containing '/' or ending in a known extension) -> kind='path_prefix', strip trailing '/*' and '**', reject absolute paths, reject any containing '..', reject mid-path wildcards.
  - technologies: capitalized or backtick-quoted identifiers that also appear as an option title or in the outcome -> role='chosen' if the outcome mentions it, else 'rejected'. Keep this conservative; false positives are worse than misses. Deduplicate.

Worker MAY run `cargo test -p adrian-core chunker`.
acceptanceCriteria: `cargo test -p adrian-core chunker` passes
One `document` chunk is always produced per ADR, even for an ADR whose sections are all empty
An `option` chunk contains the option title AND all of that option's pros/cons bullets in one chunk (asserted on a fixture whose pros_cons join requires option_key)
Chunk ids are identical across two runs on the same input (asserted)
No emitted chunk has empty or whitespace-only text (asserted over the whole fixture corpus)
An oversized section produces multiple chunks that together contain every input word, with `truncated` set only when an indivisible unit exceeds the budget (asserted with a stub token counter)
Scope extraction rejects absolute paths, paths containing '..', and mid-path wildcards (asserted)
Chunk text for `document` kind equals the source bytes exactly when under budget (asserted)

    dense_rotation [768,381] F32   <-- ALREADY PRESENT, do not recompute QR
    latents [512,768], norm_x.{weight,bias} [768], norm_latents.{weight,bias} [768]
    to_q.weight [768,768] (no bias), to_kv.weight [1536,768] (no bias), to_out.{weight,bias} [768,768]

CONFIG NOTES (these will bite you):
  - config.json has global_rope_theta: null and local_rope_theta: null. Deserialize as Option<f64> and default to 160000.0 and 10000.0. Candle's own modernbert::Config uses plain f64 and will fail to deserialize.
  - hidden 768, layers 22, heads 12, intermediate 1152, layer_norm_eps 1e-5, local_attention 128, global_attn_every_n_layers 3, max_position_embeddings 8192
  - shared_layers = 18, so the token top is layers 18..22 + final_norm, and the dense top is dense_layers 0..4 + dense_norm

FORWARD PIPELINE (transcribe exactly; this mirrors branched_transformer.py and hybrid_tokens.py):
  1. tokens: prepend [CLS]=50281 then [Q]=50368 for role=query or [D]=50369 for role=document, append [SEP]=50282.
     Truncate to 256 total tokens for role=query, 2048 for role=document. Use the tokenizers crate with tokenizer.json.
     The `[Q] ` and `[D] ` entries in tokenizer.json are single added tokens with ids 50368 and 50369 (they include a trailing space); look them up rather than string-matching.
  2. hidden = norm(tok_embeddings(ids))
  3. run layers 0..18 -> trunk
  4. token_states = final_norm(run layers 18..22 over trunk)
  5. dense_states = dense_norm(run dense_layers 0..4 over trunk)
  6. Attention: full attention for layers where i % 3 == 0, sliding window (window 128) otherwise. Use the same masking convention as candle-transformers/src/models/modernbert.rs (prepare_4d_attention_mask + get_local_attention_mask). RoPE theta 160000.0 for global layers, 10000.0 for local layers.
  7. LAP pooling over dense_states: refine(x) = x + to_out( SDPA( q=to_q(norm_x(x)), k,v = to_kv(norm_latents(latents)) ) ) then x + ff(norm_ff(x)), where ff = Linear(768->6144) then GEGLU(a,b)=a*gelu(b) then Linear(3072->768). SDPA is unmasked, scale 1/sqrt(96), 8 heads of head_dim 96. Then pooled = masked mean of refined over real tokens, then L2 normalize -> [768].
  8. token path: u = normalize( linear(token_states) @ local_rotation ) then normalize again; token_vector = [sqrt(1-0.9)=0.31622777, sqrt(0.9)*u ] -> 128 dims.
  9. dense path: g = pooled @ dense_rotation -> [381]; view as 3 slices of 127; L2-normalize each slice; slot_vector_s = [ -sqrt(1-0.225)=-0.88034084, sqrt(0.225)*slice_s ] -> 128 dims.
  10. output vector list = [slot_0, slot_1, slot_2, token_vector_2, token_vector_3, ...] i.e. slots OVERWRITE output positions 0,1,2.
  11. role=query: drop every output vector whose position >= 64 (query_local_cap). role=document: keep all.
  12. Return `dense` = the pooled 768 vector (unit norm, before rotation) so callers can build a separate dense index.

tasks.description: Ingest pipeline, Qdrant collection management, and the background embed worker
tasks.contract:
Wire the pieces into a working write path and index in crates/adrian-core.

INGEST (crates/adrian-core/src/ingest.rs):
  ingest(project_slug, external_ref, source_bytes, source_format, actor, declared_scopes) -> IngestOutcome
  1. sha256 the source. If (project, external_ref) exists with the same source_sha256, return Unchanged with the existing adr id.
  2. If (project, external_ref) exists with a different hash, create a new revision (rev+1), set tx_to on the previous revision, update adr.cur_rev, re-run parse/chunk, insert new sections/items/chunks and enqueue embed jobs. Return Revised.
  3. Otherwise parse, chunk, insert as rev 1, return Created.
  4. If the parsed front matter status maps to the closed status vocabulary, record an initial status_event; otherwise default to `proposed` and add a warning.
  5. Merge declared_scopes (origin='declared', confidence 1.0) with extracted scopes (origin='extracted'), deduplicating on (kind, value) and preferring declared.
  All inside one transaction. Enqueue one embed_job per chunk with state='pending'.

IDEMPOTENCY: ingest is called through a wrapper that consults ingest_request on (project_id, idempotency_key). Same key + same request sha -> replay stored response. Same key + different sha -> return a Conflict error mapped to HTTP 409.

QDRANT CLIENT (crates/adrian-core/src/qdrant.rs) using reqwest against ADRIAN_QDRANT_URL:
  - ensure_collection(name): create if absent with
      vectors: {
        "colbert": { size: 128, distance: "Cosine", multivector_config: { comparator: "max_sim" } },
        "dense":   { size: 768, distance: "Cosine" }
      }
    then wait until the collection reports green via GET /collections/{name}.
  - upsert_chunk(point): PUT /collections/{name}/points with payload
      { adr_id, project_id, number, rev, chunk_id, chunk_kind, option_key, template, status, model, model_version, chunk_version: 1 }
    and NO chunk text in the payload. Point id is uuid v5 over `chunk_id||model||version`.
  - delete_adr_points(adr_id): delete by payload filter on adr_id (used when a revision supersedes).
  - update_status_payload(adr_id, status): set_payload over a filter on adr_id.
  - search(project_id, query_vectors: Vec<[f32;128]>, dense: [f32;768], limit) implementing two-stage retrieval:
      stage 1: POST /collections/{name}/points/query with using="dense", query=dense, limit=200, filter on project_id
      stage 2: same endpoint with using="colbert", query=query_vectors, limit=max(limit*5, 50), filter on point ids from stage 1
    If stage 2 returns an error containing "prefetch" or the API rejects the id filter, fall back to a single-stage colbert query and log a warning.
    Return Vec<ScoredChunk { chunk_id, adr_id, score }>.
  - All calls retry 3 times with exponential backoff on 5xx and connection errors.

EMBED WORKER (crates/adrian-core/src/worker.rs):
  A tokio task started by `adrian serve` when ADRIAN_WORKER=1 (default 1).
  Loop: claim up to 16 pending embed_jobs -> batch them by role (always 'document' in v0.1.0) -> POST /v1/embed to ADRIAN_EMBEDDER_URL -> on success record chunk_vector and upsert the Qdrant point, mark job done -> on failure increment attempts and set last_error; after 5 attempts mark 'failed'.
  Sleep 250ms when no work. Must shut down cleanly on SIGTERM, finishing the in-flight batch.
  Log a warning if the embedder reports `truncated: true` for any chunk.

RECONCILE: `adrian check` subcommand that walks SQLite and reports (does not fix) chunks with no chunk_vector row, embed jobs in 'failed', and Qdrant point counts per collection. Exit non-zero if any discrepancy is found, so it can be used in CI.

result:
Built Adrian v0.1.0, a self-hosted ADR database: a three-container compose stack (adrian / qdrant / embedder) on network `adrian` with only Adrian publishing a port.

**What works end to end.** A MADR document goes in over REST or MCP, is parsed into a typed projection with byte spans, chunked along the template's own structure, embedded by a from-scratch candle engine, and indexed in Qdrant as a ColBERT multivector plus a dense vector. Retrieval has three arms: dense candidates reranked with an exact MaxSim over the model's own token matrix, FTS5 lexical search, and structured scope filtering. The two ranked lists fuse with reciprocal rank fusion. `scripts/smoke.sh` runs the whole thing against the real stack and passes.
